question: Which region has the highest average perceptions of corruption?
query: SELECT regional_indicator, AVG(perceptions_of_corruption) AS avg_perception FROM world_happiness_report GROUP BY regional_indicator ORDER BY avg_perception DESC LIMIT 50;
raw_results:
| regional_indicator | avg_perception |
| --- | --- |
| Central and Eastern Europe | 0.8709147957385894 |
| South Asia | 0.807924430197917 |
| Sub-Saharan Africa | 0.7879775342847385 |
| Latin America and Caribbean | 0.7845122361838002 |
| Commonwealth of Independent States | 0.770348861494318 |
| Middle East and North Africa | 0.7686763339857137 |
| None | 0.7671247341320756 |
| Southeast Asia | 0.7384625278959998 |
| East Asia | 0.7166281647105263 |
| Western Europe | 0.5585103714208747 |
| North America and ANZ | 0.4527128221363635 |
answer:
Based on the query results, Central and Eastern Europe has the highest average perception of corruption at 0.87 out of 1 (where 1 would be perfect transparency). This region shows significantly higher perceptions compared to other regions, with South Asia being the second most transparent in this sample.

Note: Values represent normalized scores between 0 and 1, where higher values indicate stronger perceptions of corruption.
